comment: The premise set for the EMPTY axis, declared here rather than derived, because a derived set changes under the sweep and a sweep whose population moves cannot be compared with its own previous run. Each entry names a file this repository's gates read as their population, and the empty form that is a LEGAL state of it. Zero bytes is the empty form of a markdown register: nothing in the grammar of these files forbids a register with no entries, which is exactly why a gate's reassuring sentence over one is so cheap to produce.
why_this_axis: tools/gates/premise-differential.mjs removes the repository. An absent premise crashes and gets looked at. An empty one prints a sentence the reader already expected, at exit 0 (Ursa/security, 2026-11-09: check-closures over a zero-byte docs/ideas.md printed `0 marker(s) in 0 document(s), all resolved and all closed` and ci-checks took it at passExit 0 and 2). Absent and empty are two premises and only absent was swept.

premise.why: The ledger, 602 entries on main. Ursa/security measured the zero-byte case on this exact file, so it is the row with ground truth behind it.
The incident register. Two seats append to its tail and three register tools key on its headings.
The ADR register. tools/registers/check-ids.mjs reads it for identifier collisions, which is a count that is legal at zero.
The largest register this seat keeps. A heading sweep over it is the shape that merges the whole file as one block when a pattern stops matching.
The host-facts register, keyed by section number. Cited by every charter in the roster, so a gate that reads it for citation integrity has an empty-at-zero answer.
The improvement register HQ's console parses. tools/seat/read-dates.mjs counts its entries and its read dates, and both counts are legal at zero.
HQ's vendored lessons register. Named here because a vendored file that arrives empty from a sync is the real-world way this premise goes to zero without anybody deciding it.

not_swept.what: *.baseline.json and the gate registry's own JSON
not_swept.why: Zero bytes is not the empty form of a JSON document, it is a parse error, which is the ABSENT premise the repository axis already sweeps. The legal empty form differs per schema -- {"entries":[]} here, {"rows":[]} there -- so emptying them correctly means reading seven schemas, and a wrong empty form would grade a parse failure as an empty-premise finding. Named rather than swept, and counted in the ungraded total.

not_swept.what: the board store and the forge
not_swept.why: Not files. Their empty form is a 200 with an empty collection, which is a third axis and needs a stub server rather than a worktree. Ursa/security's credential axis is the nearest existing reading of it.
